newsitem.title: USA: United Center owners pitch stadium plan - papers.
newsitem.headline: United Center owners pitch stadium plan - papers.

text.p: The owners of the United Center in Chicago have floated a proposal to build a $250 million privately financed outdoor stadium for the National Football League Chicago Bears to reduce competition for events at their arena, Chicago newspapers reported Wednesday.

Partners Jerry Reinsdorf and William Wirtz, who also own the Chicago Bulls basketball team and the Chicago Blackhawks hockey team, respectively, pitched the proposal to the Bears and legal counsel for Gov. Jim Edgar on Monday, the Chicago Tribune and Chicago Sun-Times said.
The stadium would be located adjacent to the McCormick Place convention center south of downtown Chicago where Edgar has proposed building a $500 million domed stadium, the newspapers said.
The Bears would be required to contribute $175 million toward a dome under the governor's proposal and much less under the open-air stadium plan, the newspapers reported.

But an Edgar aide in charge of the dome talks chafed at the speculation and Bears officials stated simply that they had no knowledge of the proposal and continued to focus on a multipurpose facility in Chicago, the newspapers said.
